Before using growth analysis for data analytics, you need to clarify the demands for data and plan the data access plan, and the R & D engineer completes the data access implementation according to the data access plan. The Growth Marketing Suite SDK is a self\-developed event tracking tool for basic data collection and growth marketing analysis. This article introduces you to the data access capabilities and general access processes for growth analytics.

<span id="6f3c28bb"></span>
# Data flow description

Before data access, you need to have a general understanding of the type and flow of data collected by Finder before and after data collection.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

Of which:


* Behavioral data: that is, the data collection scheme formulated according to the analysis business goals, event tracking is carried out at the corresponding location, and when the user triggers a key event, the event tracking report will be sent to the background.

* User data: collected user ID\-related data used to uniquely identify users, as well as user characteristics\-related data required for post\-business analysis.

* Device data: ID data collected to uniquely identify the device, as well as data related to device characteristics required for post\-business analysis.

<span id="3ec1c7e5"></span>
# Event tracking verification

DataFinder provides you with **real\-time event tracking detection** function. When you perform data access operation for the first time, you can test and report data through real\-time event tracking detection to verify the data reporting results. It is usually recommended to **wait 10 to 15 minutes** for data report result verification, especially the first reported event/attribute result verification.


* When accessing event tracking data for the first time, please refer to the . Perform access verification.

* You can also directly simulate the operation in the application for data reporting, and then verify the reported results. At this time, it is recommended to check and verify through the following two major directions:

   * Before the simulation report, according to the configuration points of the access SDK of each application, check again whether the code configuration of the access SDK is wrong. For the inspection points, please refer to the [1. Integrated verification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Event_Tracking_Verification_Operation_Guide#3403f53d)in the general event tracking verification operation guide document.

   * Access SDK code configuration is correct, you can **10~ 15 minutes later** , in DataFinder's metadata management, user scrutiny, analysis tool module to verify the data reported results, check points can be found in the general event tracking verification operation guide document [2. System data verification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Event_Tracking_Verification_Operation_Guide#e596a7d8)


For event tracking verification of some special scenarios, such as the H5 scenario embedded in the APP, see [3. Special scenario verification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Event_Tracking_Verification_Operation_Guide#582f0aa5)

# Product logic: data reporting & caching strategy

<span id="1e80ed67"></span>
## Data reporting strategy


|**SDK** |**Reporting policy description** |**Is it configurable?**  |**Can it be automatically adjusted according to the network environment?**  |**Can it be reported in time periods?**  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Android |* When the SDK is not initialized, if there are events triggered (including preset and custom), it will be cached in the client side memory, up to 300 caches. See the **Data Caching Policies** section below for more details on caching policies.<br><br>* After the SDK is initialized, if there is an event triggered (including preset and custom), whether init is called, after init (automatically start after default init) will drop the library, and it will be reported every 60s after starting (up to 1600 items each time, if more than 1600 items are generated in one minute, you need to wait for the next 60s to report).<br><br>* After the SDK is initialized, if you switch users, report it immediately. |No<br><br>Trigger the reporting task every 60 seconds, each request packs 200 event tracking, Android reports up to 8 consecutive requests per task, iOS reports up to 10 consecutive requests per task |No |No |
|iOS |* The SDK is not initialized and will not be cached locally.<br><br>* After the SDK is initialized, if there is an event triggered (including preset and custom), whether init is called, after init (automatically start after default init) will drop the library, and it will be reported every 60s after starting (up to 2000 items each time, if more than 2000 items are generated in one minute, you need to wait for the next 60s to report).<br><br>* After the SDK is initialized, if you switch users, report it immediately. |No |No |No |
|HarmonyOS |Default is reported once a minute, but there is no specific number of reports, SDK strategy for the new reporting strategy by volume query events (Android/iOS query by the number of queries), each report query about 1M data to report, no longer 200 shall prevail (can be reported as much as possible). |No |No |No |
|Web JS |Real\-time reporting, but there is an asynchronous queue waiting time of about 30ms. If the number of events triggered within 30ms is less than 20, they will be combined into one report. If there are more than 20 events, they will be reported separately in groups of 20. max_report can set the number of bars. |Configurable maximum number of reports and asynchronous queue wait time:<br><br>max_report: 10 (the number of combined reports defaults to 10)<br><br>reportTime: 30 (Time interval for event reporting to asynchronous queue, default 30ms) |No |No |
|Mini Program<br><br>(WeChat/Byte/Alipay/Baidu/QQ, etc.) |Default real\-time reporting.<br><br><br>* 1.X version: Support to open enable_storage. After opening, it will be reported by default every 5 seconds and up to 5 pieces each time.<br><br>* Version 2.5 and above: Support enable_buffer (buffering), enable_cache (caching).<br><br>   Buffer words:<br><br>   * buffer_interval: Default 5 seconds, can be adjusted<br><br>   * buffer_number: Default 5, can be adjusted |Configurable whether to turn on, number of seconds per interval, and threshold number of times per session<br><br>Only 2.5.0 and above versions support:<br><br><br>* enable_buffer: true//open buffer<br><br>* buffer_interval: 5000//buffer interval, in milliseconds, the default value is 5000<br><br>* buffer_number: 5//Maximum number of buffers, default 5<br><br>* enable_cache: true//open cache |No |No |
|Mini game<br><br>(WeChat/ByteDance/Quick Games, etc.) |Mini Program ||||
|fast application |Mini Program ||||


<span id="863eb662"></span>
## Data caching strategy


|**SDK** |**Data processing mechanism after network abnormalities, crashes, etc. cause failure to report** |
|---|---|
|Android |* Event tracking generated before sdk initialization will not store db, and up to 300 items will be cached.<br><br>* After initialization, the event tracking package will be stored in db, and the event tracking cached before killing the process will be dropped from the library.<br><br>* If the report is successful, it will be deleted from the db, and if the report fails, it will not be deleted from the db. It will not be deleted until the 30\-day expiration date. The db storage amount follows the mobile phone storage space. That is, DB data is retained for a maximum of 30 days. |
|iOS |The event tracking package will store the SQLite3 database. If the report is successful, it will be deleted from the database. If the report fails, it will not be deleted from db. iOS will not delete local data. SDK has no storage limit, and db storage follows the hard disk size limit of the mobile phone. |
|HarmonyOS |The event tracking package will store the database. If the report is successful, it will be deleted from the database. If the report fails, it will not be deleted from the db. HarmonyOS will not delete local data. There is no storage limit for sdk, and the db storage follows the hard disk size limit of the mobile phone. |
|Mini Program |Default reporting fails, in the case of enabling cache (1.x version parameters enable_storage, 2.5 and above parameters enable_cache), it will be put into the local storage and wait for the next supplementary reporting (a single key allows storage of the maximum data length of 1MB, all data storage limit is 10MB). |
|Web |Default no mechanism, can be configured to turn on the global<br><br>Use enable_storage: true to enable global configuration. Data that fails to report when the network is abnormal will be stored in localstorage. The next time you visit the page, the data in localstorage will be checked first, and if any, it will be sent. (The number of cache limits does not exceed 50 by default, you can use the storage_num parameter to configure the number of limits) |


<span id="c20bf6e2"></span>
## Data reporting compression strategy


|**SDK** |**Whether to compress** |**Compression algorithm for request reporting** |**Is the algorithm customizable?**  |
|---|---|---|---|
|Android |Yes |AES encryption + gzip compression |Yes (AES + CBC is supported by default, which needs to be matched with the server level) |
|iOS |Yes |AES encryption + gzip compression |Yes (AES + CBC is supported by default, which needs to be matched with the server level) |
|HarmonyOS |Yes |AES encryption + gzip compression |Yes (AES + CBC is supported by default, which needs to be matched with the server level) |
|Mini Program |No |without |without |
|Web |Yes (enable_zip needs to be turned on during initialization) |Gzip compression |without |
